why: RJ-X62 (suite/cli-bundle CB-3, pending CB-7): connect an AI assistant to the downloaded app. CB-3 writes the check and CB-7 enables it, so `platforms` is empty and the harness skips it on both platforms until then. input/launcher.suitehelp is the launcher's Help document; CB-7 runs it for a bundle at /Applications/AfterGlow.app on macOS against the assembled .build/apps/AfterGlow.app, whose Contents/Helpers/afterglow scripts/bundle-apps builds, signs and runs with --version. The job: help.connect-assistant returns the command an MCP client runs and the JSON block for clients that take one; CB-7 then starts that command and sends initialize and tools/list over stdio. The trap: the command points into the source tree, or at an unsigned binary that Gatekeeper stops. The assertion: the command's path is inside the bundle, quoted as one word, and starts the stdio server; codesign --verify passes on it; tools/list returns at least one tool for each of the five apps.
